summary: Queues (main, global per QoS, serial), groups, work items, QoS, delayed and leeway submission and a memory-pressure source are covered by bifrost_app::dispatch. DispatchSource (other than memory pressure), DispatchIO, DispatchData, semaphores, barriers, workloops, target queues, dispatchPrecondition and dispatch_once have no counterpart in the SDK.

features.note: closures run on the app loop thread via an eventfd; dispatchMain() has no counterpart because the app loop owns the thread
one shared pool with per-QoS lanes, width capped at available_parallelism
FIFO; label is kept for debugging
sync returns T; sync from the main thread onto main panics instead of deadlocking silently

Wave 2 (theme-34, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. use DispatchWorkItem::wait or DispatchGroup::wait
takes a Duration, not DispatchTime or DispatchWallTime; leeway is supported

features.apple: DispatchGroup: init, enter, leave, notify, wait
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs:468 (DispatchGroup), :471 new, :475 enter, :479 leave, :497 notify, :507 wait
features.note: wait takes an optional timeout and returns bool
cancel stops an item that has not started; no flags such as assignCurrentExecutionContext or noQoS

features.apple: DispatchQoS: userInteractive, userInitiated, default, utility, background, unspecified
features.note: four levels: UserInteractive, UserInitiated, Utility, Background; no default or unspecified; no QoS inheritance

Wave 2 (theme-29, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. docs/bifrost-ui.md:1095 lists no barriers; use a serial queue or a Mutex
handler runs on the given queue; no cancel, so the handler lives for the process; it never fires without PSI

features.feature: Other dispatch sources (timer, read, write, signal, process, file system)
features.apple: DispatchSource (activate, suspend, resume, cancel, setEventHandler, DispatchSourceProtocol)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/fswatch.rs (FSEvents-style stream, poll-based, not a DispatchSource)
features.note: no timer source (async_after_leeway covers one-shot timers); no fd or signal sources; no suspend, resume or cancel
file and descriptor I/O uses std::io on the caller's thread or the pool; no channel with low and high water marks

Wave 4 (theme-12, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. buffers are Vec<u8> or Bytes; no sparse or concatenated dispatch data type

Wave 2 (theme-29, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. docs/bifrost-ui.md:1096 says use std::sync or a group instead; decided, not missing by accident
a Darwin scheduling object for kernel-priority workloops; no Linux counterpart is planned

features.bifrost: std::sync::OnceLock is used directly in springboard/sdk/src/url.rs:168 and springboard/sdk/src/process_info.rs:189; no SDK wrapper
features.note: one-time initialisation works through std, but there is no dispatch_once API and no precondition check on queues
wait timeouts are Durations; no wall-clock time type and no timeout result enum

gaps: DispatchSource beyond memory pressure: no timer, read, write, signal or process sources, and no cancel, suspend or resume (docs/bifrost-ui.md:1095)
Barriers on concurrent queues and target queues (setTarget)
dispatch_once and dispatchPrecondition wrappers (std::sync::OnceLock is used directly)
DispatchSemaphore (docs decide on std::sync or a group instead)
DispatchWorkloop is Darwin-only (n/a); DispatchQoS default and unspecified levels are not exposed
Doc inconsistency: docs/bifrost-ui.md:1095 says there is no DispatchSource, but springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs:744 provides one memory-pressure source; the doc should say so
